hints.title: Bring the power down first
hints.body: The power law gives log10(31−n)=(1−n)log103. Every term now contains the same factor log103.
hints.recap: A logarithm turns an exponent into a multiplier.
hints.pitfall: The exponent <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> multiplies the whole logarithm. It does not become <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mi>n</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: Use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><msub><mi>log</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> before trying to add the terms.

hints.title: Check the first and last terms
hints.body: Substitute the first and last summation indices into the coefficient expression. Count how many indices occur, including any term whose coefficient happens to be zero.
hints.recap: The starting index determines the first term.
hints.pitfall: The final index and the final coefficient are different quantities.
hints.pause: Determine the first coefficient, last coefficient and number of terms before using a sum formula.

recall.reminder: Read the terms before choosing a sum: substitute the first and last indices.

hints.title: Use number of terms times the mean of the ends
hints.body: Use the number of coefficients multiplied by the mean of the first and last coefficients. Keep the resulting sign, then restore the common logarithmic factor.
hints.recap: An arithmetic sum is its number of terms times the mean of its first and last terms.
hints.pitfall: A zero-valued term still occupies a position when you count a consecutive arithmetic block.
hints.pause: Evaluate the arithmetic sum and express the original sum using the common logarithm.

recall.reminder: For a consecutive arithmetic block, count the terms carefully and average its endpoints.

solution:
The logarithm power law gives log10(31−n)=(1−n)log103.

Thus the required sum is (0−1−2−⋯−99)log103. The coefficient sum is 1002(0−99)=−4950.

The result is −4950log103. Answer A.
knowledgePattern: Logarithmic power rule converts sum to an arithmetic series
